content:
Not all power banks are created equal. Some are impressively designed, featuring onboard displays, the ability to charge two MacBooks at once, RGB lighting, and even metal enclosures with windows that expose the internal components — Sharge's new Shargeek 300 power bank is genuinely exciting, and you definitely want to check it out while the launch discount is on. Here's my hands-on impression.

Sharge Shargeek 300 Power Bank Review

The brand-new Sharge Shargeek 300 power bank features a unibody metal construction, packs a 24,000mAh battery capacity, and can deliver up to 300W of power to your devices. The semi-transparent design, RGB lighting, and onboard display are highlights, and it's currently on sale at Amazon for as low as $199.

Feature rundown:

  • 300W total output — charge 2 laptops + 1 smartphone simultaneously
  • CNC aluminum alloy chassis with advanced thermal management
  • 24,000mAh battery capacity — fully airline compliant
  • Dual USB-C, USB-A, plus adjustable DC output (5V–28V)
  • Stable power for Starlink, portable fridges, soldering irons, camera monitors, LED fill lights, and other DC-powered devices
  • 140W USB-C input — Shargeek 300 goes from 0% to 100% in just 44 minutes
  • Full-tab battery cells — operating temperatures reduced by up to 35%
  • 1.9-inch smart display with Sentinel BMS — real-time charge/discharge curves, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage history, and estimated time remaining

9to5Toys Take

In my book, Sharge is a criminally underrated brand. Their charging products look phenomenal, and the new Shargeek 300 power bank is a perfect example.

This thing is absolutely gorgeous. Not everyone will love this slightly cyberpunk-style transparent aesthetic that exposes the internals, paired with RGB lighting and an onboard display, but I personally love it, and I'm sure you'll fall for it once you see it in person.

It's a unibody CNC metal construction — most power banks with displays out there use plastic enclosures… I genuinely dread those things, but I absolutely love Sharge's design. It's as solid as a tank.

By my standards, this thing is ridiculously stylish — it would absolutely qualify as a decorative piece sitting in my office.

This brand has never let me down, never had a single issue, and honestly, if you haven't noticed them yet, you really should. I've been using this brand-new Shargeek 300W power bank for about the past month, and it's been more of the same.

As for the output power distribution, there's 300W total. With all three USB ports in use, the two main USB-C ports can each output 140W simultaneously, while the legacy USB-A delivers an additional 20W of power. I think charging three devices simultaneously is more than enough, as I rarely need more than one or two when I'm out and about.

Sharge says that charging with USB-C1 or USB-C2 alone can take your MacBook Pro from "0% to 50% in roughly 25 to 30 minutes." I've tested it, and the numbers match perfectly — my 14-inch Pro went from nearly dead to over 50% in just 27 minutes.

Alright, let's talk about this display. I genuinely love the vibe — it has this retro yet ultra-modern feel to it that I'm completely obsessed with.

Feature-wise, it pretty much has every piece of information you'd ever need to know, plus plenty more you didn't — real-time charging status, discharge curves that I don't really care about but love staring at, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage history, and all sorts of other information. Everything seems to work great from what I've seen, and more importantly, every time I pull it out for use, it gives me this Blade Runner or Cyberpunk 2077 vibe.

For power enthusiasts and serious pros alike, the way it puts charging and voltage analytics to good use makes it the most comprehensive suite of power data I've ever seen on a consumer-grade power bank.

Alright, I've found my new favorite power bank. It performs as well as it looks, and it will remain a part of my daily kit for the foreseeable future.
